title: Cabaret shows at the Plantation and May Alix's gangster tips
summary: Entertainers sang table to table and tips were split with the band; the singer May Alix did splits for gangsters who threw money.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I mean, you see, I'm going to say something. I can be a lot wrong. See, you know, a cabaret was called a night of frivolity, you know?

And the light, they never had a dull moment in them places. When the show was off, there'd be a couple of girls singing to the tables. You know, they'd sing to this table and move around, you know? And they split, not no half, they split individually with the band. Oh, yeah? If there were eight men in the band and the two girls, they'd split ten ways. Oh, yeah?
And I mean, we made some money. And you know who was the most honest to work with? Who? May Alex. May Alex.
Did she own the place? No. But she sang? So I didn't dance her then. Did she dance to May Alex?

Sure, did she? And she had gangsters in the plantation. This was doing King Oliver's reign. And one gangster on this side and one on this side, making her do the splits. They'd throw money on the floor and she'd run on up to the front and make the splits all the way back to the back of the bandstand. To the front of the bandstand. Oh, yeah. And then another one would throw money on the other side. I think she gave us $175 that night. Put the money in the tablecloth and carried it upstairs.
Gave us $175. She had to build for dear about five years ago. You know, and she would sing.
